preamble: Loss of the voiceless bilabial fricative [ɸ] is the last stage of the weakening of *p. Its best-known case is Proto-Celtic, where Proto-Indo-European *p became *ɸ and then disappeared word-initially and between vowels in all attested Celtic languages (*ɸlānos 'full' > Old Irish lán, Welsh llawn; *ɸlitanos 'broad' > Gaulish Litana, Old Irish lethan). Whether an intermediate *h stage came between *ɸ and zero is disputed: the only evidence for it is the name Hercynia, if that name is Celtic. Japanese medial ɸ was also lost, but there it went through w first, so that case belongs under phi_to_w and w_to_empty.

examples.to: Old Irish lán, Middle Welsh llawn
examples.note: Word-initial *ɸ is lost in both Goidelic and Brittonic.

examples.to: Old Irish nïa, Old Welsh nei (Welsh nai)
Old Irish lethan, Middle Welsh llydan
Litana (in the forest name Litana silva)
examples.note: Continental Celtic shows the same loss of initial *ɸ.
